title: Immunization Record Standard - Credit Window for Earlier Series Doses
content:
**Kestrel Records and Compliance - Immunization Record Standard, Immunization Services: the credit window**

**Standard.** When a patient resumes a series on a new course, earlier doses are looked for within a credit window counted back from today in whole calendar months. The credit window is 240 months where the earlier course's doses from dose 1 to the latest dose span more than 365 days, 120 months where they span 365 days or less, and zero months where the earlier course holds no dose 1.

## Definitions used by this standard

- **Dose 1 date.** The date of the dose entry numbered dose 1 on the earlier course; where the course holds more than one such entry, the most recent of them.
- **Latest dose date.** The date of the most recent dose entry on the earlier course, whatever its dose number.
- **Span.** The calendar days from the dose 1 date to the latest dose date.
- **Within the credit window.** An entry lies within a credit window of N months when fewer than N whole calendar months separate its date from today. A whole calendar month is completed on the same day number of the following month; an entry dated today lies within any window of one month or more, and nothing lies within a window of zero months.

## The window by span

| Earlier course | Span from dose 1 to the latest dose | Credit window |
|---|---|---|
| Holds a dose 1 | More than 365 days | 240 months |
| Holds a dose 1 | 365 days or less | 120 months |
| Holds no dose 1 | Not applicable | 0 months, so no entry lies within it |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- *Hypothetical.* Dose 1 on 1 March of one year and the latest dose exactly 365 days later: the span is 365 days, which is "365 days or less", so the window is 120 months.
- *Hypothetical.* The same dose 1 and a latest dose 366 days later: the span is more than 365 days, so the window is 240 months.
- *Hypothetical.* An earlier course whose only dose entry is its dose 1: the span is 0 days, so the window is 120 months.

## Whole-month counting (hypothetical dates)

With today on 15 June of a given year and a window of 120 months, an entry dated 16 June ten years earlier lies within the window (119 whole months have passed), while an entry dated 15 June ten years earlier does not (120 whole months have passed, which is not fewer than 120).
